newsitem.title: USA: Stocks edge lower ahead of Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Stocks edge lower ahead of Fed meeting.

text.p: Stocks fell Tuesday as investors sifted through new economic data to get a clue as to whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates at its policy-making meeting next week.

At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 13.60 points at 6,841.88. In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a 14-8 margin on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 257 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index was off 4.81 points at 1,274.62. The American Stock Exchange index fell 0.03 point to 596.21.
"The big worry is that we are shifting into overdrive, entering a boom-bust trajectory," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment strategist at First Albany Corp.
"That means that the economy gets too strong, the Fed is required to cool its by raising interest rates and invariably they raise rates too high and a recession follows," he said.
February housing starts reported on Tuesday came in stronger than had been expected, Johnson said, gaving the Fed, the nation's central bank, more ammunition to justify a rate hike.

The Commerce Department said builders broke ground on new homes and apartments at the fastest clip in nearly three years during February. Total starts jumped 12.2 percent to an annual rate of 1.53 million, the strongest since March 1994, after a revised 0.7 percent gain in January.
Fed policy-makers are to meet on March 25 and there is a growing conviction on Wall Street that they will raise short-term interest rates.

"The question is much deeper than just whether the Fed will raise rates," Johnson said. "The worry is that the economy is starting to accelerate and that a rate increase will be the first in a series which lead to the end of the bull market and the economic expansion."
The bond market was steady, with the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury at Monday's close of 6.96 percent.

Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at Amas Securities, said the stock market was rocky and investors lacked confidence. She pointed to the effect of investment guru Warren Buffett's recent comments that most stocks were overvalued.

"The fact that he moved the market to the extent that he did yesterday does not speak well of the market's view of itself," Farley said. She said that an interest rate hike would be a "disaster" for markets.
"The rates the market gives us are not justified by the economy. A hike would also strengthen the dollar, which is not good for us. Rates would go up, earnings down," she said.
Micron Technology Inc., the most active NYSE issue, fell 3-1/4 to 40-3/8 after the company reported disappointing quarterly results.
Harman International Industries Inc. lost 11-3/4 to 34-1/4, a day after the maker of high-fidelity audio products warned of a drop in quarterly profits.
